The Maiduguri Zonal Directorate of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission said it arraigned one Mohammed Yunus before Justice Adamu Shehu of the Federal High Court, Maiduguri, on Tuesday. This was disclosed in a statement posted on the EFCC’s official X page on Friday, adding that the defendant was arraigned on a two-count charge of money laundering to the tune of N450m. Yunus was said to have been arrested for collecting N450m for a purported contract for the supply of goods to the World Food Programme, falsely presenting himself as having secured the contract and misappropriating the said funds for his personal use. The statement said, “Count one reads: ‘That you, Mohammed Yunus, sometime in 2025 at Maiduguri, Borno State, within the jurisdiction of this honourable court, did commit an offence to wit: money laundering by converting the sum of N450,000,000, belonging to one Habu Tijjani Bolori under the guise that the said amount represent payment for the supply of goods to be made to World Food Programme where you falsely represented yourself to have secured the said purported contract from the World Food Programme, an NGO registered in Nigeria and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 18 2(b) and punishable under Section 18(3) of the Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act 2022.’ “The defendant pleaded ‘not guilty’ to the charges when they were read to him, and counsel to the prosecution, Mukhtar Ali Ahmed, prayed the court for a trial date and to remand the defendant in a correctional centre. Muhammad, through a motion for bail, informed the court that the defendant would not tamper with any of the prosecution witnesses and had undertaken not to commit any offence if released on bail.” Justice Shehu thereafter admitted the defendant to bail in the sum of N50,000,000.00, with two sureties in like sum. “He further ordered that the sureties must be residents of Maiduguri with properties having certificates of occupancy. The certificates and international passport of the defendant shall be deposited with the Registrar of the court,” according to the statement. It added that the case was adjourned until December 1, 2026, for the commencement of trial.
